history.period: 1750 AD per one source; Ganga-era origin claimed by another (verify)
history.summary: Built by a king of the Harichandan dynasty of Nilagiri; one source (odisha360) names King Ramachandra Deva Mardaraj Harichandan and dates construction to 1750 AD, while another (orissatours) vaguely attributes its founding to the Ganga-dynasty era - CONFLICT (verify). Kalinga-style main temple and Jagamohana, with Ratnavedi enshrining Jagannath, Balabhadra, Subhadra, Sudarshan and other deities; smaller shrines of Vimala, Ganesha and Shiva in the premises. Managed for years by descendants of the Harichandan royal family, now run by an independent trust. Regarded as one of Odisha's important regional Jagannath shrines (some sources call it the third/fourth most popular Jagannath temple after Puri, Koraput's Shabara Shrikshetra and Baripada - ranking unverified).

name: Nilagiri Jagannath Temple
town_description: Nilagiri is a small historic town in Balasore district, Odisha, set at the foothills of the Swarnachuda hills about 17 km from Balasore. It was the seat of the Harichandan royal family, whose palace and gardens stand near the Jagannath Temple. The town is the gateway to nearby Panchalingeswar hill and attracts pilgrims and nature tourists year-round.

travel.road: On SH-19 at Nilagiri, ~17 km from Balasore town; road access from Balasore
